newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CSR says happy with aluminium investment.
newsitem.headline: CSR says happy with aluminium investment.

text.p: Diversified building products, sugar and aluminium group CSR Ltd said on Monday it was not considering selling its 25.2 percent stake in the Tomago aluminium smelter near Newcastle in New South Wales.
"For us it is a very attractive business," CSR managing director Geoffrey Kells told reporters at a media briefing on the company's full year results.

"We have announced an expansion of about 10 percent which will keep on lowering the costs of the smelter. We think we have a very low cost investment which is very attractive to shareholders," Kells said.

CSR earlier said earnings from its investment in Tomago and its 21 percent stake in the Gove alumina refinery in the Northern Territory fell 23 percent to A$130 million in the year to March 31. Aluminium prices fell 12 percent in the period.
Kells said the earnings fall from aluminium was partially restricted by the company's hedging programme.

CSR said earlier that both operations produced record tonnages during the year. Sales of aluminium totalled a record 143,000 tonnes but bauxite sales from Gove fell by 10 percent due to revised sharing arrangements with the company's joint venture partner, Alusuisse-Lonza Holdings Ltd.
